A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the diagnosis of regional (localized) postinfarction (PI) pericardialitis is possible with the electrocardiogram (ECG) and is more likely to occur in patients with inferior than anterior myocardial infarctions.
the electrocardiographic evolution of T-waves during postinfarction regional pericardial effusion is atypical and differs between the two sites.

we have demonstrated the presence of a localized pericardial inflammation in patients with post-infarction pericardial syndromes and have described an electrocardiographic pattern that is associated with that inflammation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electrocardiographic evolution of post-infarction regional pericardial effusion (PIPE) is highly variable, and that the presence of an atypical T wave evolution pattern (either persistently positive deflection or reversal of initially depressed deflections) should not be interpreted to mean that a patient does not have a pericardial process.
the electrocardiogram is a useful and sensitive method of diagnosing localized (regional or post-infarction) pericardial inflammation.
the atypical evolution of T-waves in postinfarction patients with localized pericardial inflammation is a very common occurrence and should be recognized as a manifestation of regional pericardiitis.
